The script alphabet without the seams

Thicker strokes, more contrast, and a set that holds together as one hand rather than two. Unicode placed bold script at U+1D4D0 as fifty-two consecutive characters, and unlike plain script none of them had to be borrowed from an older block to avoid a duplicate. Everything was drawn for the same run at the same time, which is the reason it tends to render more consistently across devices than the regular script alphabet does.

That consistency makes it the better pick for anything short and prominent: a channel description header, a birthday post, the top line of a link-in-bio page. Nothing about your font changes when you use it, since you are swapping in different characters, so there is nothing for a plain-text field to strip. There are no bold script digits, though, so a date typed alongside stays in ordinary figures.

Also searched as: bold cursive text generator, bold script font copy paste, fancy bold cursive letters.

Where Bold Script text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks in most bios, posts, display names and chat — X, Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Reddit. Watch outRefused by real-name fields (Facebook, LinkedIn's name field) and unsearchable: these are separate characters from ordinary letters, so nobody will find you by typing your name.

Bold Script questions

Why does bold script render more reliably than plain script?

Plain script has eleven letters pulled from the Letterlike Symbols block, which a font may draw from an unrelated design. Bold script is one uninterrupted run of fifty-two characters, so a font that covers the run at all covers it uniformly. You get one weight and one slope across the whole alphabet.

Can I use it in a Discord nickname?

Nicknames and server display names are plain text fields, so these characters go in the way any other text does. Two caveats worth knowing: nobody can find you by typing your real name, since these are not those letters, and plenty of servers have a rule requiring a readable, mentionable name.

Does each letter count as one character or two?

It depends who is counting. Every letter here is a single Unicode code point, but it needs two UTF-16 units to store, so a limit implemented the older way charges you double. That is why a bio fits fewer styled characters than plain ones on some sites and exactly the same number on others.
